title: WebSocket
summary: Build a raw WebSocket server, then add room broadcasts and connection heartbeats in JS, TS, Go, or C#.
overview: WebSockets keep a two-way connection open after an HTTP upgrade. Start with an echo server, then choose a variant for broadcasting across a room or detecting stale peers. Each guide includes a local browser-console client to try the server.

variants.title: Echo server
variants.summary: Upgrade an HTTP request to a WebSocket and echo text or binary frames to the sender.

javascript.introduction: Node.js ESM using only ws beyond the standard library. This is the default server for learning the handshake and message loop.

sections.heading: Prepare the project
sections.body: Create a Node.js ESM project. Save the next section as server.js, then run node server.js. The ws package handles framing and handshake details.
sections.code:
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install ws
node server.js

sections.heading: Run the server
sections.body: Start a WebSocket server on /ws. maxPayload bounds incoming messages to 64 KiB. The ws driver handles the protocol handshake and frames.

sections.heading: Try the connection
sections.body: Open the dev/lib page at http://localhost:4400, paste this into its browser console, and watch for the echoed message. Close the socket afterward.

sections.heading: Production notes
sections.body: Use wss:// behind TLS in production. Check Origin against your real frontend, authenticate before accepting an upgrade, and budget one persistent connection per client. This is an echo demo, not a message broker.

typescript.introduction: TypeScript on Node.js using ws and its type declarations. Application code stays close to the JavaScript version.

sections.heading: Prepare the project
sections.body: Create a TypeScript ESM project. Save the next section as server.ts. Compile to server.js and run it. @types/ws provides the driver types.
sections.code:
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install ws
npm install -D typescript @types/node @types/ws
npx tsc server.ts --module nodenext --target es2022 --esModuleInterop --types node --skipLibCheck
node server.js

go.introduction: Go net/http plus Gorilla WebSocket for the protocol upgrade and frames.

sections.heading: Prepare the project
sections.body: Create a Go module, add the small Gorilla WebSocket driver, save the next section as main.go, and run it. net/http supplies the HTTP server.
sections.code:
go mod init example.com/ws-demo
go get github.com/gorilla/websocket
go run .

sections.heading: Run the server
sections.body: Upgrade /ws using Gorilla WebSocket. The local Origin allowlist matches the browser test page, and SetReadLimit bounds incoming messages.

sections.heading: Try the connection
sections.body: Open the dev/lib page at http://localhost:4400, paste this into its browser console, and watch for the echoed message. Close the socket afterward.

sections.heading: Production notes

csharp.introduction: ASP.NET Core WebSockets are built into the shared framework. No WebSocket NuGet package is needed.

sections.heading: Prepare the project
sections.body: Create an ASP.NET Core empty app, replace Program.cs with the next section, and run it. WebSocket support is part of ASP.NET Core; no NuGet package is needed.
sections.code:
dotnet new web -n WsDemo
cd WsDemo
dotnet run

sections.heading: Run the server
sections.body: ASP.NET Core handles the upgrade with no additional package. Forward each received fragment with its EndOfMessage flag; the browser reassembles the message.

sections.heading: Try the connection
sections.body: Open the dev/lib page at http://localhost:4400, paste this into its browser console, and watch for the echoed message. Close the socket afterward.

sections.heading: Production notes
sections.body: Use wss:// behind TLS in production. Check Origin against your real frontend, authenticate before accepting an upgrade, and budget one persistent connection per client. This is an echo demo, not a message broker.

variants.title: Broadcast rooms
variants.summary: Group peers by room and broadcast each message to everyone in that room.

javascript.introduction: Build on the echo server when one client message needs to reach other connected clients. Keep room membership local for a single-process example.

sections.heading: Prepare the project
sections.body: Create a Node.js ESM project. Save the next section as server.js, then run node server.js. The ws package handles framing and handshake details.
sections.code:
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install ws
node server.js

sections.heading: Run the server
sections.body: This server validates a room name during the HTTP upgrade, tracks peers in a Map, and removes them on close. The sender also receives its own broadcast.

sections.heading: Try the connection
sections.body: Open the dev/lib page in two browser tabs. Paste the snippet in both; messages appear in the same room only. Change one tab to room=other to see isolation.

sections.heading: Production notes
sections.body: This in-memory registry works in one server process. For multiple instances, route broadcasts through a broker and define room authorization. Cap room count, queue sizes, and per-client output; a slow peer must not hold other broadcasts indefinitely.

variants.title: Heartbeat and reconnect
variants.summary: Detect half-open sockets with protocol ping/pong and retry browser connections with bounded backoff.

javascript.introduction: Add liveness detection when connections may silently die behind mobile networks or proxies. The browser demo adds reconnect with capped backoff.

sections.heading: Prepare the project
sections.body: Create a Node.js ESM project. Save the next section as server.js, then run node server.js. The ws package handles framing and handshake details.
sections.code:
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install ws
node server.js

sections.heading: Run the server
sections.body: The server sends a ping every 30 seconds. A missing pong by the next tick causes terminate(); ws and browsers send pong frames automatically.

sections.heading: Try the connection
sections.body: A browser replies to protocol ping frames automatically. This small client retries with capped exponential backoff if the connection closes. Call stop() to end the demo.

sections.heading: Production notes
sections.body: Protocol pings are not exposed to browser JavaScript; the browser responds automatically. Retry only while the page still needs updates, add jitter for large fleets, and reload missed data after reconnect because WebSockets do not replay messages.
